## 🌎 Major world changes
The global energy architecture is bifurcating under regional conflict. With Brent crude trading above $111, European nations are absorbing over €100 billion in trade friction, triggering domestic political crises and street riots in France. Concurrently, Western military deployments—such as the UK moving air power directly into Saudi Arabia—demonstrate that traditional defense alliances are being remobilized strictly to safeguard commercial shipping lanes and hydrocarbon corridors.

## 🛡️ Scams & safety alerts
- **The "Digital Arrest" Phone Scam:** A retired judge in India was defrauded of **₹2.5 crore** after receiving a fake Skype video call from fraudsters impersonating CBI and Mumbai police officers claiming an illegal parcel was registered in his name. [[The420.in]](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiYkFVX3lxTE9JaFFITFJRaWNiTnhzVFhvM2dkM0QzVWN2VUUyWXp3aXJUVjN0ZVZaaFd2UkRqb3NaSDZRUElNUVYtQlhoekpNMkE4ZW5ET2hIRmRzanEyb1BxQmNYa3g5M0pR?oc=5)

## 🎓 Today's lesson
**Anchor Investors in an IPO:**
Before an Initial Public Offering (IPO) opens to the general public, underwriters offer a dedicated portion (up to 60% of the institutional quota) to large, high-reputation institutional buyers called **anchor investors**. These include sovereign wealth funds, major mutual funds, and pension funds. Anchor investors must bid at a fixed price and agree to a **lock-in period** (they cannot sell their allotted shares for 30 to 90 days after listing). For everyday investors, watching the anchor book—such as Jio Platforms attracting ₹2.5 lakh crore in bids for an ₹8,110 crore book—shows how much genuine confidence smart-money institutions have in the company’s valuation.
